title: Spread, Rest and JSON
summary: Copying and merging with ..., collecting with rest parameters, and JSON in and out.

steps.title: Spread
body: `...` **spreads** an array or object into a new one. It is the everyday way to copy and to update without mutating:
Later properties win, so put overrides **after** the spread. This is C#'s `record with { Size = 14 }`, and it is exactly how React state updates are written.
Spread copies are **shallow**: nested objects are shared, not cloned. For a deep copy use `structuredClone(obj)`.

steps.explain: Properties are applied left to right and the last one wins. `base` itself never changes.
The copy has its own `name`, but `tags` is the same array in both objects: spread is shallow.

steps.title: Rest
body: The same `...` on the receiving side **collects** the rest:
function sum(...nums: number[]): number {     // like C# params int[]
for (const n of nums) t += n;
`for (const n of nums)` is JavaScript's `foreach`. (`for...in` loops over **keys**; avoid it for arrays.)

steps.explain: On the right of `=` or in a call it spreads; in a parameter list or a destructuring pattern it collects.

steps.title: JSON
body: JSON is the text format web APIs use, and it looks like JavaScript object literals with quoted keys.
const text = JSON.stringify({ id: 1, done: false });   // '{"id":1,"done":false}'
const back = JSON.parse(text);                         // an object again
- A `Date` becomes an ISO **string**, and `JSON.parse` does **not** turn it back into a `Date`.
- `JSON.parse` throws on invalid text, so wrap untrusted input in `try`/`catch`.
- `JSON.parse` returns `any` in TypeScript: the compiler cannot know the shape. Validate it (module 5).

code: const s = JSON.stringify({ id: 1, note: undefined, score: NaN, tags: ["a"] });
steps.explain: `undefined` is skipped and `NaN` has no JSON form, so it becomes `null`.

steps.title: Safe settings loader
prompt: Write `loadSettings(json: string)` that parses a JSON string of settings and merges it over these defaults:
- Keys in the JSON override the defaults; missing keys keep the default.
- If the text is not valid JSON, return the defaults unchanged (do not throw).
starter: type Settings = { theme: string; fontSize: number; autosave: boolean };
solution: type Settings = { theme: string; fontSize: number; autosave: boolean };
const defaults: Settings = { theme: "light", fontSize: 14, autosave: true };
template: Dojo.eq("overrides fontSize", { theme: "light", fontSize: 18, autosave: true }, loadSettings('{"fontSize": 18}'));
Dojo.eq("overrides two keys", { theme: "dark", fontSize: 14, autosave: false }, loadSettings('{"theme":"dark","autosave":false}'));
Dojo.eq("empty object keeps defaults", { theme: "light", fontSize: 14, autosave: true }, loadSettings("{}"));
Dojo.eq("invalid JSON keeps defaults", { theme: "light", fontSize: 14, autosave: true }, loadSettings("{oops"));
hints: `{ ...defaults, ...JSON.parse(json) }` merges with the parsed values winning.
